title: Boing Voyage
blurb: Bounce a springy ball through 5 worlds, chaining epic combos
controls: A/D or ←/→ steer · Hold ↑/Space super-bounce · ↓ ground-pound · Touch
keywords: bouncing ball bouncy platformer bounce springs combos worlds bosses skins jump physics cute
prompt: Boing Voyage (Platformer). You play as a springy rubber ball named Pip bouncing through a hand-painted world, inspired by the satisfying ball-bouncing games on portal sites but entirely original. The ball always bounces automatically on landing; the player steers left/right (A/D, arrows, or on-screen touch halves) and can hold to "squish" for a charged super-bounce or tap down for a fast ground-pound that slams through cracked blocks. Physics must feel springy and weighty: real momentum, air control with inertia, visible squash-and-stretch on every impact, wobble on wall-bounces, and a camera that eases and leads. The world is full of bounce toys: spring pads, angled bumpers that ricochet you, conveyor walls, jelly blocks that absorb, sticky honey, wind fans, cannons that fire you, portals, crumbling platforms, spikes and rolling enemies you can stomp. Chaining bounces without touching the ground builds a combo multiplier with escalating pitch and particle bursts; wall-bounce chains and stomp chains score extra. Each level has stars/gems to collect, three hidden golden bolts, and a finish flag with a 3-star rating for time, gems and no-hit. Make at least 5 worlds (e.g. Toybox Meadow, Candy Caverns, Clockwork Factory, Frosty Peaks, Storm Sky) of 8 levels each plus a boss level per world where you bounce on the boss's weak spots, every world introducing two new mechanics. Collected gems buy unlockable ball skins (12+, each with its own bounce sound and trail: beach ball, bowling ball that bounces lower, golf ball, slime, disco, planet, etc.) on a skin shelf. Add a world map with animated path, achievements (20+), and a daily "Bounce Gauntlet" endless mode with a best score. Art: soft painterly 2D with layered parallax, warm lighting, cute wiggly eyes on Pip that react to speed, fear and joy. Save world/level progress, stars, gems, skins, settings and best scores under gamebop.boing-voyage.

title: Tilt Palace
blurb: Six themed pinball tables, boss toys, multiball and wizard modes.
controls: ←/→ or Z / / flip · Space plunge · Shift nudge · Touch
keywords: pinball arcade flippers ball tables multiball jackpot bumpers ramps physics retro high score
prompt: Tilt Palace (Arcade). A pinball game with a fully original set of themed tables and accurate, satisfying ball physics: a heavy steel ball with real gravity on a slanted playfield, continuous collision so it never tunnels, flippers with proper flip impulse so you can cradle, post-pass and aim shots, slingshots, pop bumpers that kick hard, ramps, orbits, spinners, drop-target banks, a kickback, and a ball save. Controls: Left/Right arrows or Z / slash for flippers, Space or Down to plunge with a pull-back meter, Shift/T to nudge the table (too much = TILT); on touch, left half/right half flip and swipe up to plunge/nudge. Each table has a mission system: light lanes and targets to start modes (multiball, jackpot hunt, timed ramp frenzy, "wizard mode" after all missions), shown with icons and a dot-matrix style animated display, not text. Start with one table and unlock at least 4 more by reaching score goals (e.g. Haunted Lighthouse, Volcano Temple, Deep-Space Dock, Circus After Dark, Clockwork Dragon), each with its own layout, toys, music loop and a boss toy that reacts when hit (a dragon that opens its jaw, a ghost ship that rises). Juice is critical: flashing inserts, lamp shows, screen shake on bumpers, slow-mo on a ball save, sparks, combo callouts, ball trails. Progression: per-table high scores, table-mastery stars, 25 achievements, unlockable ball finishes, and a daily challenge table with a modifier. Art: rich glossy 2.5D playfield rendered on canvas with lighting, reflections on the ball, chrome rails and backbox art, portrait-friendly so it looks great on a phone. Save unlocks, high scores, settings and achievements under gamebop.tilt-palace.

title: Kickflip Alley
blurb: Flip, grind and manual huge combos across sunset city spots
controls: Arrows · Z ollie · X flip · C grab · Touch joystick + 3 buttons
keywords: skateboard skating skate kickflip grind tricks combo sports sunset city ramps
prompt: Kickflip Alley (Sports). A side-scrolling skateboarding game where a skater with fully procedural limb animation (crouch anticipation before an ollie, arms balancing, hair and shirt lagging behind, bails with ragdoll-ish tumbles) rolls through hand-drawn city spots. Push to gain speed, hold and release to ollie (longer hold = higher pop), and in the air press direction + trick button combos for kickflips, heelflips, shove-its, 360 flips, grabs and spins; land on rails and ledges to grind (balance meter), hit ramps and quarter-pipes for big air, and do manuals between lines to keep the combo alive. Landing needs the board roughly level: sketchy landings wobble, bad ones bail. Scoring uses a combo multiplier that grows with variety (repeating the same trick scores less), so players invent long lines. Each spot (Rooftops, Harbour Docks, Mall Plaza, Storm Drain, Neon Night, Mountain Bomb Hill and more, at least 6) has 10 goals shown as icons: score targets, collect hidden S-K-A-T-E letters, grind a specific rail, gap challenges, a race against a rival skater, and a "trick spelled out" challenge. Completing goals earns cash and unlocks new spots, tricks, special moves (when the special meter fills), boards, wheels, outfits and stat points (pop, speed, balance, spin). Include a 2-minute free session mode with best-score saves and a daily line challenge. Controls: keyboard (arrows + Z/X/C), and touch with a joystick + 3 buttons. Art: clean vector-comic style with warm sunset palettes, parallax, people and pigeons reacting, sparks on grinds, dust on landings. Save progress, cash, gear, stats, goals and best scores under gamebop.kickflip-alley.

prompt: Junction Jam (Puzzle). A real-time train-routing puzzle on a charming miniature railway diorama. Coloured trains roll out of tunnels and must reach the station of the same colour; the player taps switches (junctions) to flip them, with a satisfying clunk animation, and can tap a train to brake it briefly. Trains have real-feeling motion: they accelerate, lean on curves, puff steam, couple carriages that follow along the track with lag, and collisions cause a cartoon crash with sparks and a slow-mo moment that ends the attempt. Each level is a hand-designed layout that introduces something new: crossings, timed level-crossings with cars, one-way spring switches, colour-painting sheds that change a train's colour, swap tracks, bridges that rise for boats, double-length freight trains, express trains that never brake, night levels where only lit sections are visible, and a build phase in later worlds where you place a limited number of track pieces before pressing Go. At least 60 levels across 6 regions (Meadow Valley, Seaside, Mountain Pass, Desert Canyon, Snowy North, Big City) on a winding map, each scored 3 stars by perfect deliveries and speed, plus an endless "rush hour" mode where trains spawn faster and faster, with a best score. Earn tickets to unlock train liveries, station decorations and a diorama you can decorate with your collected props. 20+ achievements. Art: tilt-shift toy-model look, soft shadows, little trees swaying, people waving on platforms, day/night lighting. Controls: mouse/touch tap; keys 1-9 also flip numbered switches.
